newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PIRATES RALLY IN NINTH TO BEAT BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PIRATES RALLY IN NINTH TO BEAT BRAVES.

text.p: Turner Ward's one-out single scored the tying and go-ahead runs and Al Martin also had a two-run single in a four-run ninth inning as the Pittsburgh Pirates rallied past the Atlanta Braves, 5-2 on Tuesday.
"I'm up there with a 3-0 count and I knew he was going to come right after me, and I was aggressive at the plate and I hit a line drive up the middle," said Ward.
"You prepare and do everything you can," said Braves manager Bobby Cox. "You either do it or you don't. We've got a lot of don'ts right now."
Clint Sodowsky (2-2) recorded the final two outs of the eighth for the win.

At Colorado, Matt Beech allowed four hits over seven innings to finally earn his first victory of the season and Rico Brogna went 3-for-4 with two RBI as the Philadelphia Phillies blanked the Colorado Rockies, 5-0.
Beech (1-7) walked none and struck out six to win for the first time in 16 starts this season.
"I'm just so happy that I won the ballgame," Beech said. "At this pace, I'll be a 20-game winner in 18 years."

In Houston, Mike Hampton allowed two runs over seven innings for his seventh straight win, and Chuck Carr had three hits, including a solo homer, and three runs to lead the Houston Astros to their fourth consecutive victory, a 13-2 rout of the Florida Marlins.
Hampton (10-7) gave up five hits while issuing a career-high seven walks and striking out six.
The Astros have scored 40 runs and have banged out 52 hits during their four-game winning streak.

"It's a little but surprising because we don't expect to get it from all those guys," Houston manager Larry Dierker said. "Their track records don't tell us that it should happen, but in baseball we should never be surprised, no matter what happens."
Florida's Al Leiter (8-9) surrendered seven hits and eight runs in four innings."

In Los Angeles, Jose Hernandez hit a two-run homer to snap a seventh-inning tie and Mark Clark allowed two runs in six innings in his Cubs' debut as Chicago snapped a nine-game road losing streak with a 4-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

With one out in the seventh, ex-Dodger Dave Hansen singled to centre and Hernandez followed with his fifth homer, driving a 1-1 pitch from starter Hideo Nomo (11-9) over the centre-field fence for a 3-1 lead.
Nomo yielded four runs and seven hits over 6 1/3 innings and suffered his first loss since July 16th.
In San Diego, Greg Vaughn had three RBI, including a two-run double that snapped a seventh-inning tie and propelled the San Diego Padres to a 6-4 victory over the Montreal Expos.
Vaughn, who had a bases-loaded walk in the fourth, greeted reliever Dave Veres with double that eluded left fielder Henry Rodriguez, bringing home Ken Caminiti and Wally Joyner for a 6-4 lead.
"It was a battle up there," Vaughn said. "I just tried to wait as long as I could and I was able to get the bat on it."

In San Francisco, Wilson Alvarez allowed two earned runs over 7 1/3 innings for his first home victory as a Giant and was one of six players to drive in a run, leading San Francisco to a 7-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
Alvarez (2-1), acquired from the Chicago White Sox in July, went 7 1/3 innings, giving up three runs and seven hits with nine strikeouts and three walks.
Jeff Kent added two hits and Barry Bonds scored twice for the Giants, who got at least one hit from every starter but right fieler Stan Javier.

In St Louis, Mark McGwire drove in three runs with a homer and double and Tom Pagnozzi homered in his first at-bat in more than three months as the St. Louis Cardinals handed the New York Mets their fourth straight loss, 5-2.

McGwire posted his most productive effort with the Cardinals, hitting a leadoff homer in the fourth down the left-field line that gave St. Louis a 3-1 lead. His two-run double into the left-centre field gap off Dave Mlicki (5-9) in the fifth capped the Cards' scoring.
Pagnozzi, who had been on the disabled list since April, opened the scoring with a two-run homer in the second.
In the Mets' fourth, Todd Hundley hit his 26th homer of the season.
